Computing div_{M^{-1}}(M) gives [1/2,0], so -M∇H+div_{M^{-1}}(M) gives -2λη - (1/2)x∇G (missing +1) and has the wrong x-component. The correct drift is -M∇H plus the Euclidean row divergence of M, namely [3/2, x/(2η)], which is also what the later Fokker-Planck computation uses.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: standard theory (Bakry--Emery criterion, Holley--Stroock theorem) applies to the potential $\frac 12 \lambda \|\vec x \|^2+G_3(\vec x)$, as it is a bounded perturbation (given by $G$) of a convex potential (given by $\frac12\lambda\|\vec x\|^2$).

issues.failure_explanation: The invariant measure is proportional to exp(-β(λ/2||x||^2+G_3(x))). The perturbation in the exponent is βG_3, so Holley-Stroock reduces the base Gaussian LSI constant βλ by exp(-β(sup G_3 - inf G_3)). The stated R=βλ e^{inf G - sup G} omits the factor β in the exponent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the constant to R=βλ e^{-β(\sup G-\inf G)} (equivalently βλ e^{β(\inf G-\sup G)}).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit geometric rate in theorem thm_bndd_G is too optimistic. Qualitative geometric convergence remains valid, but the stated quantitative bound is not supported.
issues.title: Missing β in log-Sobolev constant
issues.why_classification: A one-line constant correction, but it materially changes the advertised exponential rate for general β.

issues.overall_effect: The proof of convergence of the numerical invariant measure π_Δt to π for Lipschitz φ is invalid as written. The theorem is plausible and repairable, but the source argument does not establish it.
issues.title: Invalid decomposition in invariant-measure convergence proof
issues.why_classification: A central convergence theorem has a faulty proof, but the conclusion can likely be recovered with a standard corrected decomposition.
